messages:
Mia Chen: Heads-up — Aurora renewal. Procurement asked to swap a 12% discount for migration assistance (data migration + sandbox onboarding) applied on the renewal invoice. They say risk is data transfer, not price.
Ethan Lowe: Migration scope? They want 50K rows migrated, sandbox with anonymized prod data, and one onsite workshop.
Priya Singh: So procurement wants services credited on the invoice rather than a cash discount?
Mia Chen: Exactly. They want the credit to appear on the renewal invoice and for the migration to be a deliverable tied to the credit.
AJ Patel: Finance: invoice credit OK if we have clear Delivery & Acceptance milestones and a non-refundable clause. Also need to ensure revenue recognition doesn't get deferred — propose a short-term commit or net-new ARR guardrail if extension included.
Ethan Lowe: Operational ask: we'll need access to customer S3 and db dump. That raises security/data concerns.
legal-bot: We'll need a Data Transfer Addendum and explicit consent for sandboxing/recordings. Also a clause that anonymization responsibilities are agreed upfront. I'll draft a 2-paragraph addendum: "Sandbox Data Use" and "Migration Responsibilities." ETA 6h.
Priya Singh: Delivery acceptance should include: migration runbook, verification checklist, sample row counts, and customer sign-off on sandbox. That will gate the invoice credit.
Mia Chen: Procurement also asked that the migration credit be split across two invoice lines: 70% applied at renewal, 30% held until final migration sign-off. Ops — can we represent that?
ops-bot: We can create two invoice lines and apply provisional credit on the first line; final 30% released after acceptance checklist processed and PO references both lines. Require PO match and signed acceptance.
AJ Patel: If we accept split credit, add a clause: if customer cancels before final sign-off, final 30% expires. Also consider a clawback if migration causes rollback.
Ethan Lowe: Tech note: we need an agreed data retention window for the sandbox and confirmation that no PII is stored. Who owns anonymization?
legal-bot: Addendum will state vendor will perform anonymization per customer-approved script; customer must sign off on anonymization plan before data handed over. Also include indemnity carve-outs for willful misuse.
Priya Singh: I'll draft amendment text: 
`Amendment: Customer will receive a one-time invoice credit for migration and sandbox onboarding services (detailed in Exhibit A). 70% of credit applied to the renewal invoice upon execution of this amendment; remaining 30% applied upon delivery and Customer acceptance of migration deliverables (migration runbook, verification checklist, anonymization report, and signed acceptance). Credit is non-transferable and non-refundable.`
Mia Chen: Procurement also asked about payment terms — they want net60 on the delta invoice after credit. Finance — can we do net60?
AJ Patel: Net60 on post-credit balance is OK but escalate for CFO approval if >$100k exposure. I'll flag.
Ethan Lowe: Timeline: if we start handoff immediately, migration pilot could finish in 3 weeks. If so, procurement may accept the 70/30 split. If not, they want a 3-month extension + smaller credit.
Mia Chen: I'll pause countersign until legal addendum + finance guardrails are added. Priya — can you prepare Exhibit A (scope + acceptance checklist) and tentative migration dates?
Priya Singh: On it. Tentative pilot: start 06/10, sandbox by 06/17, workshop 06/21. Will attach checklist.
Mia Chen: Thanks. Once legal drafts addendum and finance signs off on net60 and clawback language, I'll send amendment and request countersignature and PO. :thumbsup:
